panel0.title: Select Records and Comparison Scope
panel0.caption:
To start, select a sequence you care about or one recognized by an experimentally identified antibody. This sequence is the antigen target. Next, you select a pool of sequences to look for molecular mimicry from; these are its potential mimicry parents. A minimum identity threshold setting defines how broad the search is.

Here, HEPACAM (GlialCAM; Q14CZ8) is the antigen target. All proteins from a set of 120 curated viral proteomes supply the mimicry parents. We search at a minimum identity of ≥5/9 and follow the HEPACAM-EBNA1 example through scoring and pairwise coverage.
panel1.title: Inspect and Summarize Results
panel1.caption:
MimicryMap produces individual sequence matches and summaries that compile those matches for reuse. The full data viewer locates qualifying nine-residue core pairs in the target and parent sequences. At a selected site, matches can be ranked by core identity (e.g., 8/9 outranking 5/9), context identity (e.g., 20/27 outranking 6/27), or BLOSUM62 score. Individual alignments and their coordinates can be inspected and exported.

To summarize all matching events between two records, MimicryMap calculates target and parent coverage. This combines qualifying nine-residue cores into independent residue unions on each sequence. Overlapping residues count once; the entire qualifying core contributes, including mismatched positions, while context flanks are excluded. These same coverage values appear in the viewer and exported summaries:

Target Coverage = 100 × covered target residuestarget length
Parent Coverage = 100 × covered parent residuesparent length

For HEPACAM versus EBNA1 alone, 21 qualifying window pairs at ≥5/9 merge into 9 + 16 + 30 = 55 covered target residues and 14 + 17 + 25 + 9 = 65 covered parent residues. Target coverage is 100 × 55/416 = 13.2%; parent coverage is 100 × 65/641 = 10.1%. These summarize all observed coordinate matches.

At HEPACAM residues 376-384, the EBV library yields 27 qualifying window pairs across 14 protein records at ≥5/9. Across all 120 viral proteomes, this becomes 293 pairs across 214 records, including two non-EBV pairs at ≥7/9.

These numerous matches illustrate why experimental evidence is essential for identifying biologically relevant mimicry. Across a library, reach counts distinct eligible target records with at least one qualifying match; pooled target coverage unions covered residues across the selected parents. Downloadable pair summaries retain matches at 7/9–9/9 with ≥10% coverage of either sequence. The Downloads page provides premade summary CSVs for mappings within and between canonical human and exposure proteomes, curated viral proteomes and assay libraries. These portable files retain identifiers, sequences, coverage values and matched residue ranges at 7/9, 8/9 and 9/9. These summaries offer a quick way to explore broader patterns of sequence mimicry, but their 7/9 minimum excludes the illustrated 5/9 HEPACAM–EBNA1 match. Focused searches at lower identity thresholds therefore remain valuable for investigating individual targets.

These downloadable mapping summaries define antigen sets for Reactivity Enrichment in SeroMap, which tests whether a sample’s recorded hits are overrepresented among antigens matching a chosen reference proteome. The worked example demonstrates individual-sample and cohort reactivity enrichment for viral peptides, and explains how the same approach applies to human autoantibody targets, using the sample’s overall assay hit rate as the expected-by-chance baseline. The pan-viral atlas uses a separate, unfiltered comparison at 5/9–9/9. Its reduced archive records the maximum identity per human window and viral protein, preserving human-side coverage and reach but not viral coordinates to reduce total size of the archive.

panel2.title: Extract Window Pairs
panel2.caption:
Each sequence contributes all overlapping nine-residue window cores. This begins with the first amino acid and ends with final complete core of nine: max(0, sequence length − 8). HEPACAM contains 416 residues and therefore 408 positional window cores; the figure shows extraction across residues 367–393. Repeated sequences retain their distinct positions.

Windows per record = max(0, record length − 8)
HEPACAM: 416 − 8 = 408 windows

An identical process is done across the entire mimicry parent library. Across the 120 included viral proteomes, there are 2,222 proteins and polyproteins, with 961,063 possible mimicry windows.

The possible search space contains every target-parent window pairing. MimicryMap uses indexes to identify candidates, then verifies their identity.

Possible Window Pairs = 408 × 961,063
= 392,113,704 ≈ 3.92 × 108 possible pairs
motif.title: Example 5/9 Patterns
panel3.title: Map Context
panel3.caption:
Each qualifying core pair is extended by up to nine available residues on either side, giving an aligned context of up to 27 residues. Context total residue identity and a summed BLOSUM62 score are available to rank qualifying core pairs.

For the selected HEPACAM-EBNA1 5/9 core pair, the flanks add only one identical position, giving 6/27 context identity and a BLOSUM62 score of 12. If the full 27 residue context is not available due to being near the start or end of the full protein sequence, missing positions contribute neither identity nor BLOSUM62 score.
panel4.title: Apply Core Threshold
panel4.caption:
Candidate windows are aligned without gaps and checked for identical amino acids. At a minimum core identity of ≥5/9, five or more corresponding positions must match. Only the 20 canonical amino acids contribute identity; other symbols retain their coordinates but count as mismatches.

The illustrated masks show five required matches; each wildcard (*) leaves a position unrestricted, so additional matches also qualify. X marks an observed difference.

For the selected HEPACAM–EBNA1 pair, XSPPRXPXX shows five identical positions and four differences. This pair qualifies at 5/9 but is just one of many possible ways mimicry may occur at this site.
